source_text: Duobus et tribus testibus etiam contra sanguinem hominis credi solet; quanto magis duobus sacris testibus, legi, quae in Deuteronomio continetur, et historiae, quae regum facta complectitur, pro Dei honore crederetur! Quomodo iudicari vellet, ipse praescripsit; quomodo, quod mandaverat, accipi deberet, secundum legem eius iudicia prolata testantur; et dubitatur adhuc traducem peccati Scripturarum probari auctoritate non posse? Certe sunt ista contraria, pro quibus tam longis conflictibus dimicatur, id est unum quod a vobis, aliud quod a nobis defenditur, et ita contraria atque repugnantia, ut vos persequendo, nos disputando, vos furore, nos ratione certemus. Utraque ergo pars distare sibi haec et repugnare consentit, id est propter parentum peccata puniri filios et propter parentum peccata filios non puniri; crimen naturale esse et crimen naturale non esse; ut parentum peccata filiis imputentur, Dei lege praescribi et, ut non imputentur parentum peccata filiis, Dei lege praescribi. Has opiniones contra semet sententiasque bellantes pariter veras non posse esse manifestum est. Nam et disputationis eruditae regulis indicatur, cum de rebus incertis opinio duplex nascitur, utramque falsam esse posse, utramque veram esse non posse; quod quidem in speciebus diversis et quae medium habere dicuntur, non tamen in his, quae contraria sunt, sed medio carent, evenire potest. Notae dialecticis res sunt, sed propter lectorem disciplinae huius expertem aliquo id reseremus exemplo.
pass_a_gloss: By two and three witnesses it is customary to be believed even against the blood of a human; how much more by two sacred witnesses, the law which is contained in Deuteronomy and the history which embraces the deeds of kings, would it be believed for the honor of God! How he wanted judgment to be given, he himself prescribed; how what he had commanded ought to be taken, judgments brought forth according to his law testify; and is it still doubted that a vine-layer of sin cannot be proved by the authority of the Scriptures? Certainly those things are contrary for which it is fought with such long conflicts, that is one which is defended by you, another by us, and so contrary and fighting that you contest by persecuting, we by disputing, you by frenzy, we by reason. Both parts therefore consent that these differ from themselves and fight, that is that sons be punished for parents' sins and that sons not be punished for parents' sins; that crime is natural and that crime is not natural; that it is prescribed by the law of God that parents' sins be imputed to sons and that it is prescribed by the law of God that parents' sins not be imputed to sons. It is manifest that these opinions and sentences warring against themselves cannot equally be true. For it is also indicated by the rules of learned disputation that when a double opinion is born concerning uncertain things, both can be false, both cannot be true; which indeed can happen in diverse species and those said to have a middle, yet not in those which are contrary but lack a middle. Things known to dialecticians, but for the reader inexperienced in this discipline let us unlock it by some example.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Two or three witnesses are ordinarily believed even in a case involving someone’s life. How much more should two sacred witnesses be believed when God’s honor is at stake: the law contained in Deuteronomy and the history recording the kings’ deeds! God himself prescribed how he wished judgment to be given; judgments delivered according to his law testify how his command should be understood. Is there still doubt that Scripture’s authority cannot establish the transmission of sin?

Surely the positions over which we fight such lengthy battles—what you defend and what we defend—are contrary. They are so opposed and incompatible that you fight by persecution and we by argument, you by fury and we by reason. Both sides therefore agree that these statements differ and conflict: children are punished for their parents’ sins; children are not punished for their parents’ sins. Guilt is natural; guilt is not natural. God’s law commands that parents’ sins be charged to children; God’s law commands that parents’ sins not be charged to children. It is obvious that these mutually hostile opinions and propositions cannot both be true.

The rules of trained argument also show that when two opinions arise about uncertain matters, both can be false, but both cannot be true. This can indeed occur in differing alternatives said to admit a middle position, but not in opposites that have no middle. These matters are familiar to dialecticians; for readers unfamiliar with this discipline, however, let us explain them with an example (Deuteronomy 17:6) (Deuteronomy 19:15).

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
